findings.summary: Future-local fragmented control and bridge reads are cancellation-unsafe when raced in tokio::select, allowing a competing branch to discard an authenticated prefix.
Pair acquisition resets retained checkpoint state to Idle, so shutdown can apply while a reconnecting checkpoint is still pending.
Pre-bridge grants and aborts are permanently rejected and ledgered instead of being boundedly deferred until the replacement bridge authenticates.
Quiescing control loss can synchronously wait for replacement authentication and miss an already queued bridge EOF.
Control FIN and RST have contradictory post-bridge shutdown meaning; after bridge authentication, only bridge EOF may prove emulator exit and one absolute quiescing deadline must bound retries.
Routine replay-ledger saturation consumes all capacity and prevents the lifecycle shutdown record.
A slow unauthenticated bridge candidate serially occupies handshake time and delays authenticated shutdown handling.
The launcher test helper has an exhaustive ControlCommand match that must handle ShutdownRequest after control protocol v2 is integrated.
